correctness.rationale: The proof gives a matching lower bound from a perfect matching, an explicit parity-class edge-resolving construction for every \(n\ge3\), separate proofs for the two boundary dimensions, and an equality argument classifying every minimum basis. Exhaustive subset checks for \(Q_1\) through \(Q_4\) and direct parity checks through \(Q_{10}\) agree with every stated value and basis count.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge searches for the exact formula, parity-class bases, vertex-cover reformulations, and stronger or equivalent hypercube coverage found the defining dominant-edge-metric paper, ordinary edge/mixed metric work on hypercubes, and later dominant-edge results for a different graph family, but no source containing the higher-dimensional hypercube formula or basis classification.

value.rationale: The result determines an infinite family exactly and, beyond the numerical parameter, identifies every minimum basis. The proof exposes a structural coincidence between the hypercube bipartition, minimum vertex covers, and edge resolution that is reusable in studying related product graphs.
